  conversation is a webview — the package contributes three webview views and no terminal at all.   
  Permission prompts and dialogs are [1mprotocol messages[0m: the initialize response carries             
  [38;5;153mpending_permission_requests[39m and [38;5;153mpending_user_dialog_requests[39m, which exist so a reconnecting client
  gets handed the prompts still outstanding. Nothing is read off a screen.                       
                                                                                                  
  [1mThe IDE WebSocket isn't that channel and can't be made into it.[0m [38;5;153m~/.claude/ide/43013.lock[39m holds a
  pid, workspace folders, [38;5;153m"ideName":"VSCodium"[39m and an auth token — the IDE hosts the socket and the 
  CLI connects [3mout[0m to it. It carries ordinary MCP with the IDE as the server: [38;5;153mopenDiff[39m,            
  [38;5;153mgetDiagnostics[39m, [38;5;153mselection_changed[39m, [38;5;153mat_mentioned[39m. That's how the CLI reaches the editor, not how it
  asks you a question. So hosting one of these wouldn't give an interactive session a structured   
  dialog channel.                                                                                   
                                                                                                    
  [1mAnd the protocol still costs the terminal.[0m [38;5;153mclaude --help[39m at 2.1.260 marks [38;5;153m--output-format[39m,        
  [38;5;153m--input-format[39m and [38;5;153m--include-partial-messages[39m each [3m"only works with --print"[0m. That's exactly what 
  MUS-D-0088 measured on 2026-08-22 and declined — still true thirteen days and several CLI versions
  later.                                                                                            
                                                                                                    
  So this isn't a parser decision. It's [1mMUS-D-0016's premise: is a Mustur session a terminal?[0m That's
  [1mMUS-Q-0076[0m, raised [38;5;153m--needed[39m because building further would be building on the answer:             
                                                                                                    
  - [1mStays a terminal[0m — nothing built is discarded, the parser finishes, and Mustur permanently reads
    dialogs off a screen that exists as structured messages three feet away.                        
  - [1mBecomes a client[0m — no scraping, no legend, nothing to misread; and nobody ever attaches to a    
    Mustur session from a machine again. A rewrite of four milestones, and it breaks MUS-D-0091's   
    vendor neutrality.                                                                              
  - [1mBoth[0m — pays for both answers, in a product with one project and one owner.                      
                                                                                                    
  [38;5;153mMUS-W-0022[39m is paused, not abandoned — the parser is correct and reads a real picker. I withdrew   
  [1mMUS-Q-0075[0m (where a prompt renders): it only matters if the prompt is scraped, and a protocol     
  dialog has a title, a body and typed options and wouldn't be squeezed into a key row.             
                                                                                                   
  The gate is red on MUS-Q-0076, deliberately. Everything else green: 1429 links, 347 identifiers.

  The panel was recommended because a picker's rows don't fit on a button, and it cost terminal
  height. The row was cheap and threw away the column where a picker says what an option [3mdoes[0m. [1mA pop
[0m  [1mup pays neither[0m — it takes the room a dialog needs because it's over the terminal, and gives it
  back on demand because the pane underneath is what you want the room for. Minimising is the answer
  to my own objection that a pop up covers what it's describing, which MUS-D-0143 says must hold.

  Built:                                                                                            
                                                                                                    
  - [1mHeld above the dock.[0m A dialog covering the composer would take the reply box away exactly when
    you want to type instead of press.                                                              
  - [1mRebuilt only when the prompt changes.[0m A screen frame arrives on every redraw and a cursor blink 
    is a redraw — rebuilding per frame would drop your minimised state several times a second. A    
    prompt that changes while minimised [3mstays[0m minimised; you put it away to read the pane, and a    
    redraw isn't a request to bring it back.                                                     
  - [1mIts buttons send the same key frame the row does.[0m One path, one allowlist, one place it can be  
    refused. The cursor's row is marked, not pre-pressed.                                           
  - [1mAnchored to the session column[0m, not the viewport, so a wide layout puts it over the terminal    
    rather than beside the rail.                                                                  
                                                                                                    
  One thing I'd assumed and now proved: the frame reads the prompt off the [1mraw[0m capture, because     
  [38;5;153mSplitChrome[39m takes the legend off with the rest of the CLI's furniture. There's a test saying so 
  rather than a comment claiming it.                                                                
                                                                                                    
  [38;5;153mreadInput[39m now resolves keys through [38;5;153mSendChoice[39m, which is what lets the picker's [38;5;153ms[39m be pressed at   
  all.
